title: Paula Jean Welden
subtitle: Long Trail · Vermont, 1946
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the forested Green Mountains of southern Vermont in early winter in the 1940s, bare hardwoods and dark spruce, grey overcast light, cold blue-grey palette with muted colour, melancholy and quiet, cinematic composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Bennington, Vermont. December first, nineteen forty-six. An eighteen-year-old college student left campus, to go hiking.
beats.img: A small New England college campus at the edge of wooded hills on a grey early-December afternoon in the 1940s, bare trees, a gravel path leading away toward dark forested mountains, no people.

beats.vo: She wore a red coat, jeans, and sneakers. Light clothes, for a December night in the mountains.
beats.img: A narrow hiking trail through bare winter woods in Vermont at late afternoon, a few dry leaves, cold low light, the last low sun throwing a faint red light along the empty path, no person.

beats.vo: Around four o'clock, hikers on the Long Trail spoke with her, near Glastenbury Mountain. No one is known to have seen her again.
beats.img: A forest trail bending around a corner into dense dark spruce and birch woods on a mountainside at dusk, light fading fast, an old wooden trail marker post with no lettering, empty.

beats.vo: Hundreds of people searched the woods. No trace of her was ever found.
beats.img: A vast stretch of dark forested Vermont mountainside in early winter seen from above, a thin dusting of snow, low cloud on the ridges, a few distant lantern points scattered in the trees.

beats.vo: Vermont had no state police. Her case led to the creation of one, in nineteen forty-seven. What happened to her has never been determined.
beats.img: An empty mountain trail in deep winter woods at blue hour, untouched snow, tall dark spruce, silent and unresolved.

facts.claim: Paula Jean Welden, 18, a Bennington College sophomore, left campus the afternoon of December 1, 1946 to go hiking (told roommate she was going for a hike/walk)
She wore a red coat/parka, blue jeans and sneakers; clothing adequate for the afternoon but not for the night's drop in temperature
Last confirmed sighting ~4 p.m., speaking with hikers on the Long Trail near Glastenbury Mountain (off Route 9); no confirmed sighting after
Hundreds of volunteers, family, National Guard and firefighters searched; extensive search found no sign of her; no body or forensic clue ever found
Vermont had no statewide police in 1946; per VSP her case 'led directly to the 1947 formation of the Vermont State Police'
Still unsolved: VSP lists it under Unsolved: Missing, 'no conclusive outcome was ever determined', with a current tip contact; no 2024-2026 reports of remains/resolution found
